pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Brown, pink, and gold
   B. Green, orange, and purple
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

2. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Remove the need for rules
   B. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   C. Guarantee a trophy
   D. Replace drinking water

3. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. Only the costume
   B. The ticket price
   C. Only the volume
   D. The speed of the music

4. Best practice when working on Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts : (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .
   B. Disrupt classmates during Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .
   C. Practise Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts  with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .

5. Best practice when working on Drawing and Painting: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Drawing and Painting.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Drawing and Painting.
   C. Practise Drawing and Painting with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Drawing and Painting.

6. Best practice when working on Melody: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Melody.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Melody.
   D. Damage equipment used for Melody.

7. Best practice when working on Indigenous Kenyan Crafts: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Indigenous Kenyan Crafts with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Indigenous Kenyan Crafts.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Indigenous Kenyan Crafts.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Indigenous Kenyan Crafts.

8. Best practice when working on Swimming: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Swimming.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Swimming.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Swimming.

9. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   C. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.

10. Best practice when working on Rugby: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rugby.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rugby.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rugby.
   D. Practise Rugby with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. Best practice when working on Athletics and Mosaic: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Athletics and Mosaic.
   B. Practise Athletics and Mosaic with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Athletics and Mosaic.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Athletics and Mosaic.

12. Best practice when working on Components of Creative Arts and Sports: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   B. Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   D. Damage equipment used for Components of Creative Arts and Sports.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Swimming and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Red, blue, and yellow

2. B — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

3. D — The speed of the music

4. C — Practise Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts  with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. C — Practise Drawing and Painting with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. A — Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. A — Practise Indigenous Kenyan Crafts with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. A — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. D — Practise Rugby with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. B — Practise Athletics and Mosaic with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. B — Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Swimming; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rhythm; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
